---
title: "Time from submission to publication"
---

## Computing time from submission to publication

Since 2015, AER and AEJ DOIs, and AER:Insights DOIs from its start in 2019, are based on the manuscript number. For example, `10.1257/aer.20151234` was submitted in 2015, as manuscript 1234 of that year. Within a submission year, the quartiles of the manuscript numbers give the *submission quarter*. Publication month is taken from CrossRef. Time is computed  from the *middle month* of that quarter to the month of the print issue. P&P are excluded (there are deterministic submission and publication months), and JEL, and JEP are excluded (different submission mechanisms). Only publication years in which (nearly) all articles come from fully observed submission years are used. The [README](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/packages-over-time#time-from-submission-to-publication) has the details.

The thread through the different analyses is: Has strengthened enforcement of the AEA's data (and code) availability policy, implemented in 2019 affected the time from submission to publication?

## Results

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
delay = FileAttachment("data/time_to_pub_articles.csv").csv({typed: true})
byYear = FileAttachment("data/time_to_pub_by_year.csv").csv({typed: true})
ks = FileAttachment("data/time_to_pub_ks.csv").csv({typed: true})
djournals = ["AER","AER:Insights","AEJ:Applied Economics","AEJ:Economic Policy","AEJ:Macro","AEJ:Micro"]
viewof dj = Inputs.select(djournals, {label: "Journal", value: "AER"})
viewof split = Inputs.radio(["Published before / from 2019", "With / without a replication package"],
                            {label: "Compare", value: "Published before / from 2019"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
dsel = delay.filter(d => d.Journal === dj)
groups = split.startsWith("Published")
  ? [{name: "Published before 2019", color: "#2F6DB5", f: d => d.year < 2019},
     {name: "Published 2019 and later", color: "#C2611F", f: d => d.year >= 2019}]
  : [{name: "With a package", color: "#1B4F8A", f: d => d.has_package},
     {name: "Without", color: "#6b6b6b", f: d => !d.has_package}]
gdata = groups.map((g, i) => ({...g, id: `hatch-${i}`, angle: i === 0 ? 45 : -45,
                              rows: dsel.filter(g.f)})).filter(g => g.rows.length > 0)
thresholds = d3.range(-6, 102, 3)
{
  // overlapping histograms, each hatched in its own color and direction (crosshatched where they overlap)
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width, height: 360, marginLeft: 50, marginBottom: 45,
    x: {label: "Months from submission to print publication", domain: [-6, 96], ticks: d3.range(0, 97, 12)},
    y: {label: "Share of articles (%)", grid: true, percent: true},
    marks: [
      ...gdata.map(g => Plot.rectY(g.rows, Plot.binX({y: "proportion"},
          {x: "months_to_pub", thresholds, fill: `url(#${g.id})`, stroke: g.color, strokeWidth: 1.2, inset: 0}))),
      ...gdata.map(g => Plot.ruleX([d3.median(g.rows, d => d.months_to_pub)], {stroke: g.color, strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "5,3"})),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  });
  const defs = gdata.map(g => `<pattern id="${g.id}" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" width="6" height="6"
      patternTransform="rotate(${g.angle})"><line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="6" stroke="${g.color}" stroke-width="2"/></pattern>`).join("");
  chart.insertAdjacentHTML("afterbegin", `<defs>${defs}</defs>`);
  const swatch = g => `<span style="display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;margin-right:18px">
      <svg width="16" height="16"><rect width="15" height="15" x="0.5" y="0.5" fill="url(#${g.id})" stroke="${g.color}"/></svg>
      ${g.name} (n = ${g.rows.length})</span>`;
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.innerHTML = `<div style="font-weight:600;font-size:1.05rem;margin-bottom:4px">${dj}: time from submission
    to publication (share of articles in each 3-month bin)</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85rem;margin-bottom:6px">${gdata.map(swatch).join("")}</div>`;
  wrap.append(chart);
  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pstr = p => p < 0.001 ? "< 0.001" : "= " + p.toFixed(3)
ksRows = ks.filter(d => d.Journal === dj &&
  (split.startsWith("Published") ? d.comparison.startsWith("Published") : d.comparison.startsWith("With")))
md`**Kolmogorov–Smirnov test** (are the two distributions different?):

${ksRows.map(d => (d.D === null || d.D === undefined)
    ? `- ${d.period}: not tested (n = ${d.n1} and ${d.n2}).`
    : `- ${d.period}: D = ${d.D.toFixed(2)} (5% critical value for these sample sizes: ${d.D_crit_5.toFixed(2)}); permutation p ${pstr(d.p_permutation_holm)}, Holm-adjusted across journals: ${d.significant ? "**different**" : "not significantly different"}.`).join("\n")}

All test statistics are in Tables 3–5 on [Methods](methods.qmd).`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div class="fig-notes">
<p>Hatched bars: share of the articles in each group whose time from submission to publication falls in each 3-month bin; the two groups are hatched in opposite directions and crosshatched where they overlap. Dashed vertical lines: medians.</p>
<p>${split.startsWith("Published") ? "Groups by year of print publication: before 2019, and 2019 and later." : "Groups: articles with at least one replication package in the AEA Data and Code Repository, and articles without one."}</p>
<p>Time from submission to publication: months from the middle of the submission quarter to the month of the print issue. The submission year comes from the manuscript-number DOI and the quarter from the manuscript number. For the AEJs, times fall on a 3-month grid (quarterly issues).</p>
<p>Sample: ${dj} articles with manuscript-number DOIs, published ${d3.min(dsel, d => d.year)}–${d3.max(dsel, d => d.year)}, in years in which the submission dates can be assigned.</p>
</div>`
```

The K-S statistic *D* is the largest gap between the two cumulative distributions. These are shares of articles, so groups of different sizes can be compared directly. The sizes enter through the critical value, which shrinks with the effective sample size *n*₁*n*₂/(*n*₁+*n*₂): with a small group, only a large gap is significant. Times fall on a grid and have many ties, so the p-value comes from 10,000 permutations of the group labels, keeping the two group sizes, rather than from the asymptotic formula.

## Mean time by year

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof view = Inputs.radio(["publication year", "submission year"], {label: "By", value: "publication year"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
yv = byYear.filter(d => d.view === view)
Plot.plot({
  width, height: 340, marginLeft: 50, marginBottom: 45,
  x: {label: `Year of ${view.split(" ")[0]}`, tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {label: "Mean time (months)", grid: true, domain: [0, d3.max(yv, d => d.hi) * 1.05]},
  marks: [
    view === "publication year" ? Plot.ruleX([2018.5], {stroke: "#44546A", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}) : null,
    Plot.line(yv.filter(d => d.Journal !== dj), {x: "year", y: "mean", z: "Journal", stroke: "#cccccc"}),
    Plot.ruleX(yv.filter(d => d.Journal === dj), {x: "year", y1: "lo", y2: "hi", stroke: "#44546A", strokeOpacity: 0.6}),
    Plot.line(yv.filter(d => d.Journal === dj), {x: "year", y: "mean", stroke: "#44546A", strokeWidth: 1.8}),
    Plot.dot(yv.filter(d => d.Journal === dj), {x: "year", y: "mean", stroke: "#44546A",
             fill: d => d.complete ? "#44546A" : "white", r: 3.5,
             channels: {n: "n", median: "median"}, tip: {format: {x: "d"}}})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<div class="fig-notes">
<p>Dark line and points: mean months from submission to print publication for ${dj}, by year of ${view.split(" ")[0]}. Vertical bars: 95% confidence intervals. Grey lines: the other journals.</p>
<p>${view === "publication year" ? "Dashed vertical line: the 2019 AEA-wide policy (between 2018 and 2019)." : "Hollow points: submission years whose articles are still being published. They miss their slowest papers, so their means are too low."}</p>
<p>Sample: articles with manuscript-number DOIs (AER, AER:Insights, AEJs), in years in which the submission dates can be assigned.</p>
</div>`
```

## How to read this

- **AER:** no change in the time from submission to publication after 2019.
- **AEJs:** times are 3–7 months longer after 2019 than before. But the increase is gradual, from 2017 to 2022, not a step at 2019. For AEJ:Applied and AEJ:Micro it starts with papers submitted in 2017. A publication backlog in 2021–22 and COVID fall in the same window. The [policy regressions](regressions.qmd) test this with placebo years.
- **With versus without a package:** AER articles with a package take about 5½ months longer, and those published before 2019 did as well (the same gap, not significant on the smaller sample). Articles without a package include those exempt from the policy (no data or code) and those whose package was not matched.
